rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours»

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2»

The underlying cause was the tank's thermostatic switches. [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC». [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed». The board report called this switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share»

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted that spacecraft was Michael Collins, the command module pilot. [[michael-collins]] «[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11».

During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia. [[michael-collins]] «[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing».

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The mailbox was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter, made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. The crew built it from radioed instructions.

- The adapter was needed because the command module's canisters were square and the lunar module's were round. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] «[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round»
- Engineers devised the adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] «[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape»
- The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] «[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions»

The notes do not say who in the engineering team devised the design or how long the build took.

rows.question: How did the Cortright report describe the switch failure?
rows.answer:
The Cortright report, the Apollo 13 Review Board chaired by Edgar Cortright, called the switch failure a serious oversight: [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share». This comes from 1970 newspaper coverage, not the report text itself.

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2». It recommended removing electrical equipment from inside the tank [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel». It also recommended redesigning the oxygen tank [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Recommended redesigning the oxygen tank and removing electrical equipment from inside it».

The switch problem itself is described in [[oxygen-tank-2]]: "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC", and "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed". The notes do not give the report's own wording on the switches.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here is the answer again, with each quote copied word for word from the fact lines, tags included:

- **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] «[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity»
- **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] «[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10» and [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting)»
- **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Launched 1970-04-11»
- **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded, about 56 hours into the flight. [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight». The same day, a Mission Control abort decision changed the goal from a Fra Mauro landing to a safe return to Earth. [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision)»
- **1970-04-17:** The crew, using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17»
- **June 1970:** The Apollo 13 Review Board report was published. It traced the fire to thermostatic switches in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Published in June 1970». The report's cause finding is cited in [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2».
